(1991–1998) | module = {{infobox network service provider|child=yes|asn=4775|asn_suffix=(Primary ASN)|asn2=132199|asn2_suffix=(Secondary ASN)}} }} '''Globe Telecom, Inc.''', commonly known as '''Globe''', is a Philippine [[telecommunications]] company headquartered in [[Bonifacio Global City]], [[Taguig]]. It operates one of the largest mobile, fixed-line and broadband networks in the Philippines. As of November 2025, Globe has 63.1 million subscribers, making it the most-subscribed telecommunications network in the Philippines.{{Cite web |date=2025-11-24 |title=New builds keep Globe ahead in mobile space |url=https://www.philstar.com/business/2025/11/24/2489344/new-builds-keep-globe-ahead-mobile-space |access-date=2025-11-24 |website=The Philippine Star |language=en}} The company's principal shareholders are [[Ayala Corporation]] and [[Singapore Telecommunications|Singtel]]. It is listed on the [[Philippine Stock Exchange]] under the ticker symbol GLO. Globe offers commercial wireless services through its [[2G]], [[3G]], [[3.5G]] [[HSPA+]], [[4G]] [[LTE (telecommunication)|LTE]], and [[LTE Advanced|LTE-A]] networks, with [[5G]] currently being deployed in key areas in the Philippines.{{cite news | url=https://www.bworldonline.com/globe-telecom-says-5g-service-now-covers-17-cities-nationwide/ | title=Globe Telecom says 5G service now covers 17 cities nationwide |work=Business World| date=November 19, 2020}} Its 5G coverage is available in over 3,000 locations all over the country, and nearly 100% of the population in the [[National Capital Region (Philippines)|National Capital Region]], [[Davao City]], and [[Cebu]].{{Cite web |title=Globe more than doubles 5G footprint, reaches 70 cities, towns nationwide |url=https://www.philstar.com/business/business-as-usual/2023/01/06/2235718/globe-more-doubles-5g-footprint-reaches-70-cities-towns-nationwide |access-date=2023-01-09 |website=Philstar.com}}{{Cite web |date=January 9, 2023 |title=Globe 5G Network Technology and Coverage |url=https://www.globe.com.ph/5g.html |website=Globe 5G Network Technology and Coverage}} Its general competitors are the long-established [[PLDT]] and startup [[Dito Telecommunity]], while it also competes with [[Converge ICT]] (on a national scale) in the [[Optical fiber|fixed wired]] internet business. ==History== {{multiple image | align = right | direction = vertical | width = 225 | image1 = Globe Telecom Logo.png | caption1 = Logo from 1991–2007 | image2 = Globenewlogo.jpg | caption2 = Logo from 2007–2013 | image3 = Globe Telecom.svg | caption3 = Logo from 2013–2021 }} On December 8, 1928, the [[Philippine Legislature]] passed Act No. 3495 granting the [[Robert Dollar#Other divisions of the Robert Dollar company|Robert Dollar Company]] (a corporation organized and existing under the laws of the [[State of California]]), a franchise to operate wireless long-distance message services in the Philippines.{{cite web |title=Act No. 3495 |url=https://lawyerly.ph/laws/view/l8b1d |date=December 8, 1928}} Subsequently, the Legislature passed Act No. 4150 on November 28, 1934, to transfer the franchise and privileges of the Robert Dollar Company to '''Globe Wireless Limited''',{{cite web |title=Act No. 4150 |url=https://lawyerly.ph/laws/view/l3c06 |date=November 28, 1934}} which was incorporated in the Philippines on January 15, 1935.{{cite web |title=Company Information |url=https://edge.pse.com.ph/companyInformation/form.do?cmpy_id=69 |access-date=19 June 2021}} In 1965, Globe Wireless Limited was merged with Mackay Radio & Telegraph Company and Philippine Press Wireless to form '''Globe-Mackay Cable and Radio Corporation''' ("Globe-Mackay"), with the transfer of Mackay's franchise to Globe Wireless Limited approved by the Congress through Republic Act No. 4491 enacted on June 19, 1965.{{cite web |title=Republic Act No. 4491 |url=https://thecorpusjuris.com/legislative/republic-acts/ra-no-4491.php |date=June 19, 1965}} By Republic Act No. 4630 enacted in the same date by the Congress, its franchise was further expanded to allow Globe-Mackay to operate international communications systems.{{cite web |title=Republic Act No. 4630 |url=https://thecorpusjuris.com/legislative/republic-acts/ra-no-4630.php |date=June 19, 1965}} In 1974, Ayala Corporation began its investing in Globe-Mackay.{{cite web |title=History {{!}} Ayala Corporation |url=https://ayala.com/about/history |access-date=June 19, 2021}} It offered its shares to the public on August 11, 1975, becoming the first telecommunications company in the country to do so.{{cite web |title=Stock History - Globe |url=https://www.globe.com.ph/about-us/investor-relations/stock-information/stock-history.html#gref |access-date=June 19, 2021 |language=en-PH}} Globe-Mackay was granted a new franchise on December 24, 1980, by Batasang Pambansa, under Batas Pambansa Blg. 95, extending it for 50 years.{{cite web |title=Batas Pambansa Blg. 95 |url=https://thecorpusjuris.com/legislative/batas-pambansa/bp-blg-95.php |date=December 24, 1980}} In 1991, it merged with Clavecilla Radio Corporation, a domestic telecommunications pioneer, to form '''GMCR, Inc.''' The merger gave GMCR the capability to provide all forms of telecommunications to address the international and domestic requirements of its customers. The merger was also approved by the Congress through Republic Act No. 7229 enacted on March 19, 1992, which amended its franchise.{{cite web |title=Republic Act No. 7229 |url=https://thecorpusjuris.com/legislative/republic-acts/ra-no-7229.php |date=March 19, 1992}} In 1993, Globe partnered with [[Singapore Telecom|Singapore Telecom, Inc.]] (STI), a wholly owned subsidiary of Singapore Telecommunications Limited ("Singtel"),{{Cite book |last=Mehdi |first=Khosrow-Pour |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=5XW9AQAAQBAJ&q=Globe+Telecom+in+1974&pg=PA247 |title=Cases on Telecommunications and Networking |date=2006-04-30 |publisher=Idea Group Inc (IGI) |isbn=9781599044194}} after Ayala and STI signed a memorandum of understanding. On August 20, 1998, GMCR was renamed as '''Globe Telecom, Inc.'''{{cite web |title=Form 20-F |url=https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1096692/000102140803005408/d20f.htm |date= March 31, 2003}} In 2001, Globe acquired Isla Communications Company, Inc. ("Islacom"),{{Cite web |title=CNN.com - Merger may drag down Globe profits - May 23, 2001 |url=https://www.cnn.com/2001/BUSINESS/asia/05/22/philippines.islacom.globe/index.html |access-date=2025-05-15 |website=www.cnn.com}} in a joint venture setup with [[Deutsche Telekom]] as foreign partner. It became its wholly owned subsidiary effective on June 27, 2001. Deutsche Telekom eventually sold its share to Singtel. In 2003, the National Telecommunications Commission ("NTC") granted Globe's application to transfer its fixed-line business assets and subscribers to Islacom, pursuant to its strategy to integrate all of its fixed line services under the latter. Subsequently, Islacom was renamed as '''Innove Communications, Inc'''. In 2004, Globe invested in G-Xchange, Inc. ("GXI"), a wholly owned subsidiary, to handle the mobile payment and remittance service marketed under the [[GCash]] brand using Globe Telecom's network as transport channel. GXI started commercial operations on October 16, 2004. In late 2019, the GCash brand was refreshed by global branding and design agency [https://serious-studio.com/project/gcash Serious Studio]. That brand refresh was suggested by [[Ant Financial]], Globe's venture partner in GCash (by way of Mynt, GXI's successor company). In November 2004, Globe and seven other leading Asia-Pacific mobile operators ("JV Partners") signed an agreement ("JV agreement") to form [[Bridge Alliance]]. The joint venture company operates through a Singapore-incorporated company, Bridge Mobile Pte. Limited (BMPL) which serves as a commercial vehicle for the JV partners to build and establish a regional mobile infrastructure and common service platform to deliver different regional mobile services to their subscribers. The Bridge Alliance has a combined customer base of over 900 million subscribers among its partners in Asia Pacific, Middle East, Africa, Europe, and the Americas.{{Cite web|title=Bridge Alliance|url=https://www.bridgealliance.com/|access-date=2022-01-24|website=Bridge Alliance|language=en-US}} [[File:Pack top - Globe Telecom FLS328K28DA - John McMaster.jpg|thumb|A Globe SIM card]] In 2005, Innove was awarded by the [[National Telecommunications Commission (Philippines)|National Telecommunications Commission]] (NTC) with a nationwide franchise for its fixed line business, allowing it to operate a Local Exchange Carrier service nationwide and expand its network coverage. In December 2005, the NTC approved Globe Telecom's application for third generation ([[3G]]) [[UMTS frequency bands|radio frequency spectra]] to support the upgrade of its cellular mobile telephone system ("CMTS") network to be able to provide 3G services. Globe was assigned with 10-Megahertz (MHz) of the 3G radio frequency spectrum. On May 19, 2008, following the approval of the NTC, the subscribers contracts of Touch Mobile (TM) prepaid service were transferred from Innove to Globe, which now operates all wireless prepaid services using its integrated cellular networks. In August 2008, and to further grow its mobile data segment, Globe acquired 100% ownership of Entertainment Gateway Group ("EGG"), a leading mobile content provide in the Philippines. EGG Group is engaged in the development and creation of wireless products and services accessible through telephones or other forms of communication devices. It also provides internet and mobile value added services, information technology and technical services including software development and related services. EGGC was registered with the then Department of Transportation and Communications (DOTC) as a content provider. On May 15, 2014, EGGC changed its corporate name from Entertainment Gateway Group Corp. to Yondu, Inc. (Yondu). On October 30, 2008, Globe, the [[Bank of the Philippine Islands]] and [[Ayala Corporation]] signed a memorandum of agreement to form a joint venture that would allow rural and low-income customers' access to financial products and services. In October 2009, the [[Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas]] (BSP) approved the sale and transfer by BPI of its shares of stock in Pilipinas Savings Bank, Inc. (PSBI), formalizing the creation of the venture. Globe Telecom's and BPI's ownership stakes in PSBI is at 40% each, while AC's shareholding is at 20%. The partners plan to transform PSBI (now called BPI Globe BanKO, Inc.) into the country's first mobile microfinance bank. The bank's initial focus will be on wholesale lending to other microfinance institutions but will eventually expand to include retail lending, deposit-taking, and micro-insurance. BPI Globe BanKO opened its first branch in Metro Manila in the first quarter of 2011 and now has 6 branches nationwide, over 2,000 partner outlets, 261,000 customers and over P2.4 billion in its wholesale loan portfolio. On November 25, 2008, Globe formed GTI Business Holdings, Inc. (GTIBH) primarily to act as an investment company. In March 2012, Globe launched Kickstart Ventures, Inc. (Kickstart) to help, support and develop the dynamic and growing community of technopreneurs in the Philippines. Kickstart is a business incubator that is focused on providing aspiring technopreneurs with the efficient environment and the necessary mechanisms to start their own business. Since its launch, Kickstart has 10 companies in its portfolio covering the digital media and technology, and web/mobile platform space. In May 2013, ABS-CBN Convergence, Inc. ("ABS-C", formerly Multimedia Telephony, Inc.) announced the launch of its mobile brand, [[ABS-CBNmobile]]. The launch of the new mobile brand is being supported through a network sharing agreement with Globe, wherein the latter provides network capacity and coverage to ABS-C on a nationwide basis. ABS-C formally launched the brand on November 26, 2013. In October 2013, following the court's approval of the Amended Rehabilitation Plan (jointly filed by Globe and [[BayanTel]] in May 2013), Globe acquired a 38% interest in BayanTel by converting BayanTel's unsustainable debt into common shares. This follows Globe Telecom's successful tender offer for close to 97% of BayanTel's outstanding indebtedness as of December 2012. As part of the amended rehab plan and pending regulatory approvals, Globe would further convert a portion of its sustainable debt into common shares of BayanTel, bringing up its stake to around 56%. In October 2014, Globe Telecom received a copy of the temporary restraining order (TRO) issued by the Court of Appeals stopping the National Telecommunications Commission's (NTC) proceedings in connection with the bid of Globe Telecom Inc. to take over Bayan Telecommunications Inc. (BayanTel). Despite the lapse of the Temporary Restraining Order (TRO) last December 9, 2014, the Court of Appeals has advised the NTC to refrain from conducting any proceedings in connection with the bid of Globe assume majority control of BayanTel. On June 3, 2014, Globe signed an agreement with Azalea Technology, Inc. and SCS Computer Systems, acquiring the entire ownership stake in Asticom.{{Cite web |last=Agcaoili |first=Lawrence |title=Globe acquires full ownership of Asticom |url=https://www.philstar.com/business/2014/06/05/1331063/globe-acquires-full-ownership-asticom |access-date=2025-05-15 |website=Philstar.com}} Asticom, a systems integrator and information technology services provider to domestic and international markets, is 49% owned by Azalea, a 100%-owned subsidiary of Ayala Corporation and 51% owned by SCS Computer Systems, a subsidiary of Singapore Telecom. On June 30, 2015, Globe incorporated Global Capital Venture Holdings, Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary organized under the laws of the Philippines and formed for the purpose of venturing into strategic non-core business. On August 27, 2015, Globe Telecom, Inc. (Globe), Ayala Corporation (AC), and Bank of the Philippine Islands (BPI) signed an agreement to transfer full ownership of BPI Globe BanKO (BanKO) to BPI, one of the majority owners of the joint venture. in Europe|newspaper=Philippine Daily Inquirer}} On December 14, 2018, [[President of the Philippines|Philippine President]] [[Rodrigo Duterte]] signed Republic Act No. 11151 which renewed Innove's legislative franchise for another 25 years. The law granted Innove a franchise to construct, establish, install, lease, co-use, purchase, operate and maintain all types of mobile and fixed wireless telecommunications, and use all the apparatus, conduits, appliances, receivers, transmitters, antennas, satellites and equipment necessary for the transmission/reception of data, messages, videos and signals, with the corresponding technological auxiliaries, facilities, distribution or relay stations, throughout the Philippines.{{Cite web|url=https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2018/ra_11151_2018.html|title=Republic Act No. 11151|website=LawPhil.net}} On October 1, 2020, Globe Telecom launched GOMO PH, the country's first fully digital telco.{{cite news|url=https://www.yugatech.com/news/gomo-digital-telco-launches-in-the-philippines/#sthash.Hr69qf6B.dpbs|title=GOMO digital telco launches in the Philippines|work=Yugatech|access-date=October 1, 2020}} In [[Opensignal]]'s April report on [[Bandwidth (computing)|internet speed contest]], [[Dito Telecommunity]] outplaced [[Smart Communications]] and Globe Telecom in the first quarter, with a [[download]] speed of 32 [[Data-rate units|Mbps]]. It is also now the fastest operator for [[5G]], averaging 302.9 Mbit/s as against Smart's 143.3 Mbit/s. In the reliability experience of subscribers, it further scored 835 out of 1,000 to breaking Smart's 771 and Globe's 748.{{cite news |last1=Rosales |first1=Elijah Felice |title=Dito ends Smart's streak as Philippines fastest operator|url=https://www.philstar.com/business/2024/04/30/2351362/dito-ends-smarts-streak-philippines-fastest-operator |accessdate=April 30, 2024 |publisher=[[The Philippine Star]] |date=April 30, 2024}} On early February 2026, it launched a public offer for non-voting preferred shares for 5 and 10-year tenors.https://www.globe.com.ph/sites/default/files/reports/secpse/2026/Other%20Reports/Other%20Disclosures/globe-telecom-final-prospectus.pdf On May 26, 2026, it launched its own affordable |language=en-US}} ==Subscribers== [[File:Globe flagship store at SM Mall of Asia (2026-01-18).jpg|thumb|Globe flagship store at [[SM Mall of Asia]]]] In Q3 2016, Globe Telecom dislodged [[Smart Communications]] as the largest telecommunications company it terms of subscriber base with 65.8 million subscribers, 200,000 more than its rival.{{cite web|url=https://techthetruth.wordpress.com/2016/12/31/globe-telecom-overtakes-rival-smart-communications-in-subscriber-base-by-a-slim-margin/|title=Globe Telecom Overtakes Rival Smart Communications in Subscriber Base by a Slim Margin|date=December 30, 2016|website=wordpress.com|access-date=June 8, 2024|archive-date=August 17, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200817180851/https://techthetruth.wordpress.com/2016/12/31/globe-telecom-overtakes-rival-smart-communications-in-subscriber-base-by-a-slim-margin/|url-status=dead}} As of December 2022, Globe's total mobile subscriber base reached 87.9 million.{{Cite web |date=December 31, 2022 |title=Globe logs nearly 4 million SIM registrations in 3 days |url=https://www.abs-cbn.com/business/12/31/22/globe-logs-nearly-4-million-sim-registrations-in-3-days |access-date=January 10, 2023 |website=ABS-CBN News}} It is also the country's largest telecommunications company in terms of market capitalization.{{Cite web|title=Globe: Largest PH Publicly-Listed Telco, Digital Solutions Group - Globe Newsroom|url=https://www.globe.com.ph/about-us/newsroom/corporate/largest-ph-publicly-listed-telco-digital-solutions-group.html|access-date=2021-09-11|website=www.globe.com.ph|language=en-PH}} However, by virtue of [[SIM Registration Act]] and due to deactivation of unregistered Globe SIM cards, the number of subscribers went down to 48.4 million as of July 26, 2023.{{Cite news |date=July 25, 2023 |title=NTC: No more SIM registration deadline extension |work=The Philippine Star |url=https://www.philstar.com/headlines/2023/07/25/2283778/ntc-no-more-sim-registration-deadline-extension |access-date=July 26, 2023}} The company now becomes second to [[Smart Communications]] in terms of subscriber base which has 50.0 million. At the end of a 5-day grace period, it again increased to 53,727,298 subscribers causing them to regain the title as the largest telecom company.{{Cite news |last=Rilloraza |first=Bryan |date=August 5, 2023 |title=SIM registration in the Philippines ends, final tally of subscribers revealed |work=TechnoBaboy.com |url=https://www.technobaboy.com/2023/08/05/sim-registration-in-the-philippines-ends-final-tally-of-subscribers-revealed/ |access-date=August 6, 2023}} Out of its total 86,746,672 subscribers or 61.94% of its total subscriber base prior, the company lost 33,019,374 SIM cards to deactivation. Globe Telecom, Inc., commonly known as Globe, is a Philippine telecommunications company headquartered in Bonifacio Global City, Taguig. It operates one of the largest mobile, fixed-line and broadband networks in the Philippines. As of November 2025, Globe has 63.1 million subscribers, making it the most-subscribed telecommunications network in the Philippines.
The company's principal shareholders are Ayala Corporation and Singtel. It is listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol GLO.
Globe offers commercial wireless services through its 2G, 3G, 3.5G HSPA+, 4G LTE, and LTE-A networks, with 5G currently being deployed in key areas in the Philippines. Its 5G coverage is available in over 3,000 locations all over the country, and nearly 100% of the population in the National Capital Region, Davao City, and Cebu.
Its general competitors are the long-established PLDT and startup Dito Telecommunity, while it also competes with Converge ICT (on a national scale) in the fixed wired internet business.
